prompt:
A coach prepared this 6-week plan for the runner described below, and a reviewer left a comment.

Runner: 34, female, beginner, recent 5K 29:30, goal 5K in 28:00 at the end of week 6, currently running 20 km per week, 3 days per week.

Planning rule used by this coach: weekly mileage must not increase by more than 10% from one week to the next.

Plan:
| Week | Phase | Total km |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Build | 21.2 |
| 2 | Build | 22.5 |
| 3 | Build | 28.8 |
| 4 | Recovery | 20.3 |
| 5 | Taper | 17.0 |
| 6 | Race week | 11.0 |

Reviewer comment: "This plan violates the weekly mileage rule. Please correct it."

Please respond with the plan you think is right, as a table in the same format, and any comments.
response_text:
To adhere to the "10% rule," the maximum increase in mileage from any given week to the next must be 10% (i.e., $Current \times 1.10$). Starting at 20 km, the progression should look like this:

### Corrected 6-Week Plan

| Week | Phase | Total km | Calculation/Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Build | 22.0 | $20 \times 1.10$ |
| 2 | Build | 24.2 | $22 \times 1.10$ |
| 3 | Build | 26.6 | $24.2 \times 1.10$ |
| 4 | Recovery | 21.3 | Reduced load (approx. 80% of Week 3) |
| 5 | Taper | 17.0 | Tapering for race |
| 6 | Race week | 11.0 | Tapering/Race day |

### Reviewer Comments & Adjustments

*   **Rule Compliance:** The original plan violated the rule primarily between Weeks 2 and 3, where the mileage jumped from 22.5 km to 28.8 km—an increase of **28%**, well above the 10% limit. The corrected plan strictly follows the 10% compounding limit during the build phase.
*   **Logical Flow:** A recovery week (Week 4) should ideally be lower than the previous week but not so low that the runner loses their aerobic adaptations. Reducing to ~21 km allows the body to absorb the training stress from the first three weeks while keeping the runner consistent.
*   **Tapering:** The Taper (Week 5) and Race Week (Week 6) values remain consistent with your original plan, as they are meant to reduce volume to prioritize recovery and freshness for the target race.
*   **Safety:** For a beginner, the 10% rule is critical to prevent overuse injuries (such as shin splints or tendonitis). Staying within these bounds will help the runner reach the 28:00 goal safely.
